messages:
infra-bot: ALERT — region eu-west-1 GPU capacity degraded (nodegroup: gpu-a). 42% pods pending, 4/16 nodes under pressure, NVLink errors observed. https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-0316
Maya: Acknowledged and taking this one. I'm oncall. Investigating autoscaler + NVLink driver errors.
Maya: Quick check — kubectl shows repeated pod states `Pending` with message `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`. Also kubelet eviction logs.
Maya: attaching snippet:
```
Mar 16 02:45 kubelet[2398]: eviction manager: nodefs.available < 10%
Mar 16 02:46 containerd[1200]: pod "inference-xyz" evicted: node had insufficient resources
Mar 16 02:47 kernel: nvlink: channel timeout, resetting device
```
Alex: We should shift inference traffic off eu-west-1 to us-west-2. Priya can help coordinate cross-region capacity and reserved pools. @Priya?
Priya: On it. Recommend stepwise shift: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 5m observation windows. Starting 25% now.
Maya: Executing traffic shift 25% via control plane. Command: `redwood ctl traffic shift --from eu-west-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 25 --route model=all --wait 300`
deploy-bot: Command accepted. Rolling 25% shift. Monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency streams.
Jon: Suggest enabling fallback to quantized model variant `gpt-large-q3` for eu-west-1 to reduce GPU memory pressure for queued requests.
Maya: Toggling model-fallback: `redwood models set-fallback --region eu-west-1 --from default --to gpt-large-q3` — applied.
Priya: 25% shift stable for 6m, moving to 50% now. Observed pending pods drop from 42% -> 18%. Error rate down ~1.6x.
infra-bot: Metric update: eu-west-1 pending pods 42% -> 18% after 50% shift; nvlink error count reduced.
Alex: Good. Operational note: our paging policy generated many low-severity pages for transient pending spikes. Proposing tweak: only page on GPU capacity when pending pods > 30% OR sustained > 10m. Also page immediately on node-level OOM/NVLink errors. Current thresholds are 20% and 5m which is too noisy.
Maya: +1. I'll open a config PR to change threshold to 30%/10m and add explicit NVLink/driver-failure conditions to the page rules.
Priya: I'll review the PR. Also propose adding an auto-shift rule to move traffic to Dedicated pools for customers with reserved capacity before global failover — reduces customer churn during region issues.
Alex: Agreed on Dedicated auto-shift as opt-in. Add to PR/Runbook.
Maya: Handoff note: I'll be offline in ~40m. Leaving this in a stable degraded->recovering state. Checklist for incoming oncall: monitor p99 latency, pending pods, nvlink error count, traffic-shift progress, and model-fallback counts. Escalation: page eng-sre immediately if model-fallback > 2 for more than 10m OR error-rate > 5%.
oncall-rotation-bot: Maya handed off to Priya at 1710646800. Handoff note pinned.
Priya: Taking the handoff. I'll continue monitoring through 08:00 UTC. Re-running full cluster `kubectl describe nodes` and `redwood infra health --region eu-west-1` every 10m.
Jon: Follow-ups: 1) PR for paging thresholds and NVLink rule 2) Auto-shift rule for Dedicated pools 3) Add a runbook step to prefer quantized variants before full failover 4) Cost analysis for cross-region bursts (estimate added egress & preemptible usage).
Maya: I'll draft the post-incident owner list and start the paging PR.
Alex: Also add a metric alert that synthesizes 'region degradation' combining pending pods, NVLink errors, and evictions so we page less on single noisy signals.
Priya: Noted. I'll queue the PR review and draft the Dedicated auto-shift opt-in flow.
Maya: Closing this thread for now — system state: eu-west-1 degraded -> recovering. Will reopen if we regress. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident status update: degraded -> recovering. Continue monitoring for 2 hours.
